name: Raja Ampat
blurb: Raja Ampat is an Indonesian archipelago in West Papua comprising over 1,500 islands known for marine biodiversity and coral reefs. Online conversation currently focuses on local conservation efforts alongside concerns regarding nickel mining and industrial expansion.

positive: Vibrant coral reefs and diverse marine species
High population density of walking sharks
Scenic limestone islands and clear waters
negative: Industrial nickel mining and expansion threats
Coral reef degradation from climate change
Displacement and impacts on local indigenous communities

quotes.text:
A tropical paradise under threat.
Thousands of unspoilt islands and a vast marine sanctuary: the Raja Ampat archipelago is home to one of the world’s greatest treasures of biodiversity. But this unspoilt natural environment is now under threat from industrial expansion.

Climate change beneath the surface.

Major disturbances to coral reefs once came every 10 years. Now it’s every 5–6.
IPCC projections: 70–90% further decline at 1.5°C of warming. At 2°C, more than 99%.

#SaveRajaAmpat #UnprotectedParadise #StopDirtyEnergy

Raja Ampat is sold as paradise.

Luxury resorts. Dive boats. Instagram sunsets.

Meanwhile, Papuans face displacement and repression, while parts of their homeland are quietly being sacrificed for nickel mining and the world's EV transition.

The reefs are famous.

The people are not.
